correctness.rationale: For λ,ω>0, κ>|η|+ω/2, ε>0, differentiated the given cubic equations in polar coordinates: rdot=r(λ−F r²), θdot=r²g, F=κ+η cos2θ+(ω/2)sin4θ is strictly positive, g=ε+ω sin²2θ>0. The radial-square angular equation du/dθ=2(λ−Fu)/g is linear with contracting affine return, yielding a unique positive attracting closed graph. Integrating dlog r around it proves λT=∫F/g and the η cos2θ and sin4θ integrals cancel exactly, yielding T=2πκ/[λ√(ε(ε+ω))]. Near each θ_j=jπ/2, angular damping ∫2F/g diverges as ε→0, forcing u(θ_j+v√(ε/(4ω)))→λ/(κ+(-1)^jη) uniformly for bounded v; g/ε→1+v². Original-time density dθ/[Tug] therefore approaches F_j/[4πκ(1+v²)]dv. Uniform u≥λ/M and g≥ε+c distance² imply O(1/R) tails beyond R√ε windows and ensure full weak convergence, weights F_j/(4κ), and standard conditional Cauchy. This is an infinite ε→0 argument rather than finite sampling.
